parameters.name: emissivity
parameters.interpretation: Effective surface emissivity for radiative loss.

parameters.name: h_flow
parameters.interpretation: Forced-convection loss gain: extra wall loss per SLPM^n_flow of nitrogen.

parameters.name: n_flow
parameters.interpretation: Flow exponent for forced convection (Nu ~ Re^n).

parameters.name: rho_cp
parameters.interpretation: Volumetric heat capacity rho*Cp of the susceptor (thermal mass per unit volume).

parameters.name: cp_T1
parameters.interpretation: Linear temperature coefficient of Cp: Cp(T)=rho_cp*(1+cp_T1*(T-Tref)).

parameters.name: k_w
parameters.interpretation: Effective axial thermal conductivity of the susceptor (lumps solid conduction plus internal radiative/gas axial transport).

parameters.name: kT1
parameters.interpretation: Linear temperature coefficient of k: k(T)=k_w*(1+kT1*(T-Tref)).

parameters.name: h0
parameters.interpretation: Baseline (natural-convection + conduction-through-insulation) loss coefficient.

parameters.name: h_T
parameters.interpretation: Temperature dependence of the loss coefficient (h grows with wall-ambient delta).

parameters.name: sigma_sus
parameters.interpretation: Effective electrical conductivity of the susceptor at Tref (300 °C). Determines the skin depth delta=1/sqrt(mu0*pi*f*sigma) and the Bessel-function EM coupling factor Im(J2(z)/J0(z)) that converts the Biot-Savart B²(x) field into induction power per unit axial length: P(x) = 2*(omega/mu0)*A_cross * sigma_coupling_factor * |B(x)|^2. Replaces the empirical 'power_scale / B2_REF' normalization with a physically grounded EM formula (matches compute_power_density in bio_savart_1d.py).

parameters.name: sigma_T1
parameters.interpretation: Temperature coefficient of susceptor conductivity: sigma(T) = sigma_sus * clip(1 + sigma_T1*(T-Tref), 0.01, 100). Negative for metals and graphitic materials (conductivity falls with temperature), which causes the Bessel coupling factor — and thus induction power — to vary with temperature.  Replaces the empirical ps_T1/ps_T2 correction with a physics-based skin-depth mechanism.

parameters.name: h_gw
parameters.interpretation: Wall-to-gas heat-transfer coefficient for the advected nitrogen field.

parameters.name: inlet_c
parameters.interpretation: Nitrogen inlet temperature at the left boundary (advection).

parameters.name: h_end_left
parameters.interpretation: Heat-loss conductance at the LEFT end face (gas inlet side) to the inlet temperature. Explains the cold upstream end despite end-peaked coil power.

parameters.name: h_end_right
parameters.interpretation: Heat-loss conductance at the RIGHT end face (outlet side) to ambient.

parameters.name: end_flow_gain
parameters.interpretation: Flow enhancement of the left end-face loss: h_end_left*(1+end_flow_gain*flow).

parameters.name: shell_C
parameters.interpretation: Lumped heat capacity of the insulation/support shell (the slow second thermal mass that produces the long within-run upward drift).

parameters.name: shell_G
parameters.interpretation: Conductance from the insulation shell to ambient.

parameters.name: shell_init_frac
parameters.interpretation: Initial shell temperature as a fraction of (mean initial wall - ambient) above ambient.

parameters.name: ambient_c
parameters.interpretation: Ambient temperature for convective + radiative loss.

parameters.name: tau_sensor
parameters.interpretation: Effective first-order thermal lag between the susceptor wall and the fiber-optic reading. In practice this lumps sensor thermal inertia, the gas column between wall and fiber, and any mounting-structure lag.  Larger values (hundreds of seconds) are physically plausible when the fiber reads the gas inside the tube rather than the wall directly. IIR: T_s[k]=exp(-dt/tau)*T_s[k-1]+(1-exp(-dt/tau))*T_wall[k].
